name: Data Structures Interview Questions
title: Data Structures Interview Questions
description: Prepare yourselves for technical interview with a carefully curated set of problems that appeared in companies like Google, Facebook, Amazon, Microsoft, Adobe, Flipkart, OLX Group, Walmart Labs, eBay, Ola, LinkedIn & more

modules.name: Basic programming - 1
modules.description: Fundamental concepts and skills in writing code. Includes variables, data types, control structures, and functions.

modules.name: Basic programming - 2
modules.description: More advanced problems on basic programming concepts.

modules.name: Arrays
modules.description: Arrays are data structures that store elements of the same type in contiguous memory locations. They allow for efficient access and manipulation of multiple items.

modules.name: Sorting
modules.description: Sorting refers to algorithms for arranging elements in a specific order (e.g., ascending or descending). It includes methods like bubble sort, quicksort, and merge sort.

modules.name: Strings
modules.description: Strings are sequences of characters used to represent text. They involve operations like concatenation, substring search, and pattern matching.

modules.name: Linkedlist
modules.description: Linkedlist is a data structure consisting of nodes, each containing data and a reference to the next node. It allows for efficient insertion and deletion of elements.

modules.name: Stacks
modules.description: Stacks are Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) data structures. They support push and pop operations, useful for tracking function calls and undo operations.

modules.name: Queues
modules.description: Queues are First-In-First-Out (FIFO) data structures. They support enqueue and dequeue operations, useful for managing tasks and buffering data.

modules.name: Binary Search
modules.description: Binary Search is an efficient algorithm for finding an element in a sorted array. It repeatedly divides the search space in half to locate the target.

modules.name: Graphs
modules.description: Graphs are data structures representing relationships between objects. They consist of vertices (nodes) and edges, used to model networks and connections.

modules.name: Trees
modules.description: Trees are hierarchical data structures with a root node and child nodes. They include variants like binary trees, used for efficient searching and organizing data.

modules.name: Hashing
modules.description: Hashing is a technique for mapping data to a fixed-size array using a hash function. It enables fast data retrieval and is used in implementing hash tables.

modules.name: Two pointers
modules.description: Two pointers is a technique using two references to traverse data structures. It is often used to solve problems with arrays or linked lists efficiently.

modules.name: Dynamic Programming
modules.description: Dynamic Programming is a method for solving complex problems by breaking them into simpler subproblems. It uses memoization or tabulation to optimize solutions.

modules.name: Bit Manipulation
modules.description: Bit Manipulation involves operations performed on individual bits of binary numbers. It is used for optimizing algorithms and low-level system programming.

modules.name: Backtracking
modules.description: Backtracking is an algorithm technique that builds solutions incrementally. It abandons partial solutions that cannot lead to a valid final solution.

reviews.review: The range of problems was excellent, catering to different skill levels and encouraging both learning and problem-solving.

For beginners starting their journey into programming without any prior knowledge, this will definitely be helpful. With the aid of AI, you can get clearer explanations. Those who already have some knowledge can also refer to these resources.
The step-by-step process is great for learning, and the explanations help me understand the lessons better. Additionally, the email notifications are excellent reminders to keep me on track.
A nice initiative to give learners the confidence that they can do anything and learn anything they want. Really nice work, Team CodeChef.
